name: SAME
objective: Quantify smoke particle sizes in low gravity and relate the size distribution to smoke generation and transport conditions, to support smoke detector design for future spacecraft.
fuel: Overheated spacecraft materials: Teflon, Kapton, cotton lamp wick, silicone rubber.
conditions: Smoke held in an aging chamber for 10 to 1800 s to simulate transport time to a detector.
measurements: Moment-method aerosol instruments, condensation nuclei counter (P-Trak), DustTrak, TEM grid samples, ISS and Space Shuttle smoke detectors.

name: SAME-R
objective: Reflight of SAME during Expedition 24 (2010) that added diagnostic measurements and expanded the test matrix.
fuel: Overheated Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone rubber, and Pyrell.
conditions: Airflow past the sample from quiescent to 8 cm/s. Smoke aging from 11 to 1800 s.
measurements: Prototype two-moment smoke detector, three moment measurements of the particle size distribution, TEM grid samples.

name: DAFT / DAFT-2
objective: Reduce risk for SAME by showing that a modified TSI P-Trak particle counter works accurately in microgravity, since the instrument normally relies on gravity to recycle its alcohol working fluid.
fuel: None. Aerosol standards created and analyzed in microgravity, plus ISS cabin air.
measurements: Modified P-Trak condensation nuclei counter, compared against a DustTrak control.

name: BASS
objective: Bridge the gap between the normal-gravity NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 flammability method, ground-based microgravity tests, and actual material flammability in microgravity, and assess how well an inert gaseous extinguishing agent puts out flames.
fuel: 41 samples: thin flat cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabric, thick flat acrylic slabs, acrylic spheres, and candles.
conditions: Small wind tunnel with airflow up to 40 cm/s, in opposed and concurrent flow. Nitrogen dilution, and a nitrogen jet used as a suppressant in some tests.
measurements: Flame appearance, growth, and spread rate from video and still images.
hardware: SPICE hardware in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)

name: BASS-II
objective: Examine burning and extinction of varied fuel samples to test whether materials burn as well or better in microgravity than in normal gravity, guiding flammability screening of spacecraft materials.
fuel: Rods, a spherical section, slabs, films, and fabric sheets, including acrylic (PMMA) and cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabric.
conditions: Small wind tunnel with airflow up to 40 cm/s, varied in speed and direction. Oxygen varied below 21% by adding nitrogen.
measurements: Flame appearance, growth, spread rate, and extinction from video, plus CSA-CP and CDM gas sensor readings.
hardware: Modified SPICE hardware in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)

name: Saffire-I
objective: Run a large-scale fire experiment in an uncrewed, expendable spacecraft to reduce the uncertainty of designing fire safety systems from terrestrial fire standards.
fuel: Sibal composite fabric (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass by weight), 40.6 cm by 94 cm.
conditions: Airflow of 20 cm/s through a large flow duct. Concurrent-flow and opposed-flow flame spread tests.
measurements: Camera imaging of large-scale flame spread.
hardware: Cygnus resupply vehicle after leaving the ISS

name: FLEX
objective: Map flammability limits of liquid fuels in microgravity, measure the effectiveness of gaseous suppressants (CO2, He, SF6), and build predictive models of combustion limits.
conditions: Chamber atmosphere diluted with suppressant gases, including very low oxygen concentrations.
measurements: Backlit and color imaging of burning droplets through extinction.
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)

name: ACME BRE
objective: Improve understanding of material flammability, extinction, and conditions for sustained burning, and assess whether existing flammability tests apply in low and partial gravity.
fuel: Gaseous fuels from a flat porous burner, emulating solids and liquids such as paper, plastic, and alcohol.
measurements: Thermal feedback (heat flux) from the flame to the burner surface.
hardware: ACME insert in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)

name: ACME CFI-G
objective: Cool flames investigation with gases. Includes the highest oxygen concentrations tested in microgravity in PSI.
fuel: Flammable gas such as propane, mixed with nitrogen in the chamber.
conditions: Oxygen-nitrogen mixture of up to 85% oxygen flowing from a spherical burner.
measurements: Unknown, not able to have been found.
hardware: ACME insert in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
